scope: Test the unresolved relationship between the 1961 teachers-organization legislative line and promulgated Law No.708 by reading the official enactment/amendment reasons, without claiming textual lineage that has not been demonstrated.

findings.claim: Law No.708 directly addressed teacher labor activity
findings.evidence: The National Law Information Center's official enactment reason for 교육에관한임시특례법 (Law No.708, effective 1961-09-01) explicitly lists as item 7 a ban on teachers' labor movement and collective acts, together with a five-year reduction of teacher retirement age.
findings.significance: This closes the weaker Pass 148 formulation that the later omnibus act was only broadly adjacent to the teachers-union question. Law No.708 itself had a teacher-labor-control component. It still does not prove that the 1961-06-21 교직단체법 was renamed, merged, or textually absorbed into Law No.708.

findings.claim: Law No.708 was a broad education-governance instrument rather than a teachers-union-only statute
findings.evidence: The same official enactment reason enumerates a temporary Ministry reconstruction advisory body, school/department consolidation and enrollment adjustment powers, compulsory-education school exchange powers, two-year education colleges, altered education-superintendent appointment rules, stronger supervisory authority over university faculty appointment, teacher labor/collective-action prohibition and retirement-age reduction, suspension of vice-principal rules below universities, a national examination condition for bachelor's degrees, and criminal penalties for specified violations.

findings.claim: The original stated purpose included private-school supervision and restoration of educational order
findings.evidence: The official enactment reason says private schools were organized as Civil Act nonprofit corporations under insufficiently active state supervision and states an aim of eliminating corruption/pathologies, restoring normal national-education order, and improving quality.

findings.claim: Law No.708 remained static until repeal
findings.evidence: Official amendment history records amendments effective 1962-04-24 (Law 1062), 1962-09-24 (Law 1157), 1963-02-28 (Law 1285), and 1963-04-11 (Law 1319) before repeal.

findings.claim: Law No.708 was repealed immediately after civilian transition in 1963
findings.evidence: National Law Information Center records repeal by Law No.1466 dated 1963-12-05, effective 1964-01-01. The repeal reason states that the special measures were considered no longer necessary after educational order had largely recovered.

findings.claim: The 1961-06-21 교직단체법 became or was absorbed into Law No.708
findings.evidence: Law No.708's teacher-labor prohibition creates substantive policy overlap, but no original June bill text or disposition record has yet established textual or procedural lineage.
